doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Calloway's Pullman car and bus travel
summary: Calloway's Cotton Club show toured for six months by Pullman and returned by Greyhound; Mona kept the driver awake.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Didn’t Calloway finally get a railroad car?

Well see Calloway’s band would be in the Cotton Club for six months. And then, they’d keep the same show in the Cotton Club for six months and then that show would travel for six months. And so we would go from here, you know, and stop, making all the little stops going down to the south, and that’s when he had a Pullman. He had this big Pullman with an extra car where all the musicians had their trunks. Milton and I, we always had lower seven berth, but then there was a car next to that, and you had your trunk, so you could just go and open, you know the trunks were open, you could get

dressed and go out. Because that way it alleviated the necessity of having to try to find places to stay and we would go to California using the Pullman. And coming back — oh and I must say Cab had his big automobile on the car, on the Pullman, it was really nice. And then coming back we would hire, he would hire a Greyhound bus, a very nice bus. We were fortunate that we never had to travel in cars like most of the other musicians in those days. They had to pile in automobiles. But Calloway was first class all the way. He was always first class. And coming back we would have a bus and we used to keep the same driver, the same bus, and work our way back down through the south and back to New York. And it’s kinda funny that we had this one bus driver for quite a long time, and instead of sleeping when he was supposed to be sleeping while the band was playing, he would be partying. So it was my job, I had to sit up in the seat right behind him and keep him awake until daybreak, and then Mr. Wright, who was the road manager, then he’d come and he would sit up there, sit up there with him and then I could go take a nap. But it was fun. It was really fun as I say, and I was always the only female traveling with the band all the time. So I was the den mother.
